bridge: Builds on M02 invariants/state machines, A01 failures and W16 transactions. The TLA+ example is a complete small model for the assigned tool; manual state enumeration is also supplied.
teaching:
Formal specification makes state, allowed transitions and desired properties explicit. A safety invariant says nothing bad happens in any reachable state. Liveness says something good eventually happens and needs additional scheduling/fairness assumptions. Proving safety does not automatically prove progress.

Model checking explores states within a specified model and configuration. A counterexample is a trace showing a violated property. A clean finite-state result establishes the property for that model, not every detail of an implementation. Refinement and implementation correspondence remain separate work.

Start with a tiny inventory state. One item is available and none spent. A Take transition requires positive balance, then transfers one unit. Stuttering permits no change. Enumerating the two reachable states by hand explains the invariant before using a tool. Do not confuse formal model checking with a live model-provider evaluation; this exercise needs no inference service.

Notation bridge: /\ means AND; a primed variable names its next-state value; <<balance,spent>> is a tuple. [] means always. [Next]_vars allows either a Next step or a step leaving those variables unchanged. Spec therefore permits stuttering, which is why it does not by itself promise progress.

The resource/tool video is assigned only for its reference orientation and proof-system explanation. Its script omits some live demo speech, so those old UI demonstrations are not required viewing. Use current official setup instructions for your operating system if you choose to install tooling; the manual exercise needs no installation. The jug video shows why a transition must also constrain unchanged variables, and how a deliberately false alleged invariant can produce a goal-reaching trace. That trace establishes possibility in the model, not inevitability in every execution.

Pouring bridge: let s and b be the current amounts in three- and five-unit jugs. A pour from small to big transfers min(s,5-b), so the next values are s minus that amount and b plus it. A pour the other way transfers min(b,3-s). This conserves water during a pour and respects both capacities. In the full-small-jug case the corrected large-jug expression is big′ = big - (3 - small); use the old small value, not the next-state value. The published errata corrects a different displayed expression; that video section is excluded.

When checking the Stock model with TLC, zero remaining stock is a deliberately allowed terminal situation. Set CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE in this exercise’s configuration to avoid treating that expected end as a deadlock defect; this does not assert liveness or justify disabling deadlock checks for other models. A type check, one successful goal trace, or the same number of states as another model does not prove equivalence. State the exact invariant, constants, state constraints and tool version, and distinguish an unperformed tool run from the manual reasoning below.
example:
---- MODULE Stock ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES balance, spent
vars == <<balance, spent>>
Init == /\ balance = 1 /\ spent = 0
Take == /\ balance > 0
        /\ balance' = balance - 1
        /\ spent' = spent + 1
Next == Take
Inv == /\ balance >= 0 /\ balance + spent = 1
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
====
TLC configuration:
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Inv
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
explanation: Reachable states are(1,0) and(0,1), plus stuttering self-loops. The guard prevents a second Take. The invariant preserves both nonnegative stock and conservation. No fairness condition requires a Take to occur, so a run that stutters forever still satisfies this safety specification.
exercise: Enumerate all reachable states manually. Remove balance>0 on paper and give a shortest invariant-violating trace. If using the linked TLA+ tooling, put model and configuration in separate files as documented and record exact version/result.
solution: Without the guard: (1,0)->(0,1)->(-1,2), violating nonnegative balance on the second Take. Manual reasoning is valid evidence for this tiny model; label any unperformed tool run honestly.
challenge: Extend initial balance to 2 and conservation total 2. Enumerate safe states and explain the extra specification needed to claim that every requested item is eventually processed.
challenge_solution: Safe states(2,0),(1,1),(0,2). Progress needs request/environment modelling and appropriate fairness/liveness requirements. An invariant alone cannot ensure an enabled transition is eventually selected.
